'''''Argyranthemum''''' ('''marguerite''', '''marguerite daisy''', '''dill daisy''') is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s belonging to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asteraceae]].  Members of this genus are sometimes also placed in the genus ''[[Chrysanthemum]]''.<ref>Webb, Philip Barker ex Schultz, Carl Heinrich Bipontinus. 1844. Histoire Naturelle des Îles Canaries 3(2.2): 245, 258–259</ref><ref>[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40019190 Tropicos, ''Argyranthemum'' Webb ex Sch. Bip.]</ref>

The genus is endemic to [[Macaronesia]], occurring only on the [[Canary Islands]], the [[Savage Islands]], and [[Madeira]].<ref name=Bramwell>Bramwell, D and Bramwell, Z (2001) Wild flowers of the Canary Islands. Editorial Rueda SL, Madrid, Spain {{ISBN|84-7207-129-4}}, 2nd edition.</ref>

''Argyranthemum frutescens'' is recorded as a food plant of the leaf-mining [[larva]] of the [[moth]] ''[[Bucculatricidae|Bucculatrix chrysanthemella]]''.

==Cultivation==
{{Main|Garden marguerite}}
Hybrids of ''Argyranthemum'' species, some involving species in related genera, are widely sold as [[ornamental plant]]s for [[Bedding (horticulture)|summer bedding]] or containers. These [[cultivar]]s produce prolific single or [[double-flowered]] daisy-like flowers in shades of white, pink, yellow and purple throughout summer.<ref name=FlorShawWats18>{{Citation |last1=Flores |first1=Anita |last2=Shaw |first2=Julian |last3=Watson |first3=John |date=2018 |title=Unpicking a daisy chain |journal=The Plantsman |series=New Series |volume=17 |issue=4 |pages=238–243  |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> In the UK climate, they are generally [[hardiness (plants)|half-hardy]], and can be grown from [[seed]] or [[cutting (plant)|cuttings]], or purchased as young plants to be planted out after all danger of frost has passed.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>
